title: First hearing a violin and big band; family singing solfeggio
summary: Sent on an errand around age eight or nine, he heard a violin and a band (possibly Ford Dabney's) at a dancing place, and recalls his family singing solfeggio and old French-African songs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And so around about 8 or 9, I was living on Virginia Avenue and George Washington Circle, (unintelligible) and she sent me to get some clothes to be washed, and on the way there was a dancing place, called it Jordan St. Mark's and I heard -- the first time -- I heard a little bit of piano playing, but I heard the violin and I was enchanted by this. I said, oh, what is that! And then I lingered a little too long and Mama was wondering what happened and why are you so late. so I said, what's that, and she said oh, that's the violin and later on I saw the big bands and I think it was -- the band

was People of Color and later I think it was Ford Dabney's band. They had big _____phones and the people they were beautiful, (unintelligible) and so that was it and my mother and my family, they would sing. Now, these people, they wasn't too strong on education, but they was singing solfeggio--- do-re-mi-fa-so-la-ti-do; they were singing and (unintelligible) so then what--
What kind of songs were they singing.

Some of them they was singing some old French songs, but they had something else, some funny words in there. It sound more like French-African or something like that and (unintelligible) and then they would answer because --
Could you sing one of them?
